text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock ticked down just 0.13% today despite oil prices holding firm around $102/barrel and U.S. refineries running at 93.5% capacity — a strong operating environment. The tiny decline suggests the market has already priced in the refiner-friendly backdrop: crude costs are elevated (especially physical delivery, which costs roughly $38 extra per barrel due to surging tanker rates), and diesel shortages are driving urgency to release global stockpiles, which should support refining margins. The stock's real momentum has been the 12.8% surge over two weeks, likely fueled by these same tight supply conditions and geopolitical uncertainty around Iran that keeps oil prices elevated.

The bigger picture is that refiner profits depend on the gap between what they pay for crude and what they sell refined products for — and right now that gap is wide. Diesel inventory sits at only 102.6 million barrels while refinery utilization is maxed out near 94%, creating the kind of supply pinch that rewards companies like Marathon that can keep the fuel flowing. Today's flat performance is just a pause after a strong run; the underlying conditions that drove the two-week rally remain in place.
